values: Himachal Pradesh MSME & Agri Scheme Guide — Sector-First Edition

Official-source research cutoff: 2026-08-23. Independently verified and corrected on 2026-08-23 — see the Corrections Log and Verification Notes sheets for every change, the source relied on and the limits of that pass. Start with a business activity, then review direct, strong, conditional and horizontal routes. Verify live intake before spending.
Open Business Navigator and filter Macro sector → Subsector → Business activity.
Prioritise Direct and Strong rows; Horizontal rows are general finance/employment/quality routes.
Read Status, Key benefit, Conditions and Sequence before planning the project.
Use Component Norms for horticulture benchmark caps and Source Register for evidence.
Take the shortlisted rows to the stated first contact, lender or portal for written confirmation.
A verified current window/route exists, but sanction and budget are never guaranteed.
Operational product, portal or registration route; appraisal and compliance still apply.
Scheme exists but access depends on allocation, target, call or written sanction.
Published period has ended; use only after an official successor/extension is confirmed.
Claims may continue for units already admitted, but do not use for a new 2026 project.
Evidence supports the scheme description, but a current public intake could not be verified.

Critical finding (revised 2026-08-23): the Himachal Pradesh Industrial Investment Policy 2019 lapsed on 31 December 2025 but has been extended repeatedly while the replacement policy remains unnotified — most recently, as reported on 18 August 2026, up to 12 October 2026. Its incentives are therefore still open to new units commencing commercial production within the extended window, but the end date moves and must be confirmed with the Single Window Clearance Authority before investment. AHIDF, PMMSY and FIDF were sanctioned only up to FY2025-26 and are marked fresh-window closed; Tea Board TDPS 2021–26 and APEDA FAS 2021–26 likewise. This workbook is a navigation guide — not a sanction letter, legal opinion or guarantee of budget.

Every change made in the 2026-08-23 verification pass — 108 entries: 44 corrections, 9 deletions of unsourceable figures, 17 status updates, 14 verified additions and 21 source upgrades — each with old value, new value, source relied on and reason.
What was checked, which claims were deleted for want of an official source, which corrections change a decision, and what this pass could not confirm.
Credit guarantee working capital and equity
Active - annual target or departmental sanction

Guarantee cover on eligible credit up to ₹10 crore per borrower, effective for guarantees approved on or after 1 April 2025 (raised from ₹5 crore). Extent of guarantee generally 75%-85% depending on borrower and facility category, subject to current rules and the annual guarantee fee.
A guarantee reduces lender loss, not the borrower's repayment obligation; the original ₹2 crore ceiling was obsolete.
Agriculture Extension Officer / Block Agriculture Office
Ask the lender to cover the eligible facility under CGTMSE; borrower does not apply directly to the Trust.
Credit guarantee working capital and equity
Active - annual target or departmental sanction
Non-corporate, non-farm micro business and permitted allied activities
Shishu up to ₹50,000; Kishore above ₹50,000–₹5 lakh; Tarun above ₹5–₹10 lakh; Tarun Plus above ₹10–₹20 lakh only for borrowers who successfully repaid a Tarun loan.
No direct subsidy; interest is lender-determined. Guarantee is under the MUDRA/CGFMU framework, not ordinary CGTMSE.
Agriculture Extension Officer / Block Agriculture Office
Apply through bank, RRB, small finance bank, MFI/NBFC or JanSamarth where offered.
Active - annual target or departmental sanction
Kuhl/community flow irrigation and eligible individual wells
100% for approved community kuhl work; 50% subsidy for eligible individual bore/shallow wells.
Water availability, technical feasibility and cost norms apply.
Agriculture Extension Officer / Block Agriculture Office
Apply through Agriculture Department before construction.
Active - annual target or departmental sanction
Orchards, nurseries, protected cultivation, mushrooms, mechanisation and post-harvest components
In Himalayan states many private-sector components receive 50% of benchmark cost; some components range 40%–75%. Caps are component-specific.
Use the 2025 MIDH cost norm and current HP action plan; do not use a generic percentage for every component.
Agriculture Extension Officer / Block Agriculture Office
Apply through Horticulture Department under the approved Annual Action Plan.
New manufacturing or service unit by eligible Himachali youth

Investment subsidy: 25% general, 30% SC/ST, 35% women/divyang; eligible plant/machinery/equipment base up to ₹60 lakh. Interest subsidy 5% for 3 years on loan up to ₹60 lakh; project cost up to ₹1 crore.
Confirm activity, age and current district target before incurring expenditure.
Agriculture Extension Officer / Block Agriculture Office
Apply through the MMSY portal/District Industries Centre (DIC), then the financing bank.
Mukhya Mantri Khet Sanrakshan Yojana (MMKSY) – crop-protection fencing
Active - annual target or departmental sanction
Solar, interlink, barbed-wire or composite fencing
Assistance is tiered by fencing type on the approved cost norm: solar fencing 80% for an individual and 85% for a group; composite fencing 70%; barbed wire / chain-link fencing 50%.
Sanction, design, vendor/specification and physical verification precede subsidy.
Agriculture Extension Officer / Block Agriculture Office
Apply to Agriculture Department before ordering/installation.
New micro manufacturing or service enterprise
Project ceiling: ₹50 lakh manufacturing, ₹20 lakh service. General: 10% own contribution and 15% urban/25% rural subsidy. Special category: 5% contribution and 25% urban/35% rural subsidy.
Hill-area classification may support special-category rates; portal and bank decide final category.
Agriculture Extension Officer / Block Agriculture Office
Apply only on PMEGP e-portal; scrutiny by KVIC/KVIB/DIC and bank.
State Mission on Food Processing – rural primary processing/collection centre
Active - annual target or departmental sanction
Rural primary processing and collection infrastructure
Location and project-component eligibility must be confirmed in the live call.
Agriculture Extension Officer / Block Agriculture Office
Apply under the State Mission through DIC/Industries Department.
Active - annual target or departmental sanction
Soil and water conservation, springshed, land development and livelihood activities in approved micro-watersheds
Support follows the sanctioned watershed DPR and community institutions; no single statewide individual percentage.
Not open statewide; asset ownership, maintenance and livelihood-fund rules depend on the local DPR.
Agriculture Extension Officer / Block Agriculture Office
Ask the Rural Development/Watershed office whether the village is inside an approved WDC-PMKSY 2.0 project.
HP Crop Diversification Promotion Project (JICA Phase II)
Irrigation, farm access, fencing, diversification and value-chain support in project areas
Support is delivered through approved subprojects and farmer groups; no single beneficiary-wide rate.
Not an open statewide reimbursement scheme.
Agriculture Extension Officer / Block Agriculture Office
Contact the project/Agriculture Department for selected locations and components.
Active - annual target or departmental sanction
Community water harvesting such as check dams and ponds
Government bears 100% of approved community work cost under departmental norms.
This is not a cash grant to an individual farmer.
Agriculture Extension Officer / Block Agriculture Office
Propose through Agriculture Department/block office; work is department-sanctioned.
Kisan Evam Khetihar Mazdoor Jeevan Suraksha Yojana
Active - annual target or departmental sanction
₹10,000–₹40,000 for specified injuries; ₹1 lakh for severe disability and ₹3 lakh for death, subject to rules.
This is accident compensation, not business capital assistance.
Agriculture Extension Officer / Block Agriculture Office
Submit claim promptly through Agriculture Department/revenue/authorised channel with incident evidence.
Active - annual target or departmental sanction
Farm inputs, cluster production, seed multiplication and agriculture-support components
Common notified input rates include 50% on seed of cereals/pulses/oilseeds/fodder and 25% on potato/ginger/turmeric; other components vary annually.
MKSY is an umbrella; use the current component circular, not a single blanket percentage.
Agriculture Extension Officer / Block Agriculture Office
Apply through local Agriculture Extension Officer/block office under the notified component.
Him Unnati / Him Krishi cluster programme
Cluster production, aggregation, services and market linkage
Need-based approved support through about 2,600 clusters; no single universal cash percentage.
Enabling programme; the sanctioned cluster DPR controls individual benefits.
Agriculture Extension Officer / Block Agriculture Office
Contact Agriculture Department to confirm whether the village/commodity cluster is selected.
Government bears 90% of implementation consultant cost; indicative programme costs: Basic free, Intermediate ₹1.2 lakh, Advanced ₹2.4 lakh, with additional support for specified categories.
The benefit is for structured LEAN implementation, not machinery purchase.
Agriculture Extension Officer / Block Agriculture Office
Register on LEAN portal and use approved implementation consultant.
PM-KUSUM / Saur Sinchai implementation in HP
Active - annual target or departmental sanction
Standalone solar agriculture pumps and notified solarisation components
85% assistance for small and marginal farmers and 80% for medium and large farmers on approved solar water-lifting/pumping systems, individual or community.
Original CSV's separate 60%/80% rows were not a reliable representation of HP's current assistance.
Agriculture Extension Officer / Block Agriculture Office
Apply through the HP AgriDBT portal (agridbt.hp.gov.in) or the dedicated PM-KUSUM portal (pmkusumagri.hp.gov.in) via the Block/District Agriculture Office.
Active - annual target or departmental sanction
Generally 40%–50% on notified equipment and benchmark cost; exact rate varies by beneficiary and machine.
Do not confuse with the central SMAM component; check the current machine-wise cost norm.
Agriculture Extension Officer / Block Agriculture Office
Apply through Agriculture Department/DBT workflow before purchase.
Active - annual target or departmental sanction
Central procuring entities target 25% annual procurement from MSEs, including sub-targets of 4% for SC/ST-owned and 3% for women-owned MSEs; tender benefits/exemptions apply under policy.
This is market access, not a cash subsidy; tender quality and technical conditions remain.
Agriculture Extension Officer / Block Agriculture Office
Register Udyam and GeM; respond to eligible tenders and use MSME Sambandh/Samadhan mechanisms.
Rajiv Gandhi Prakritik Kheti Khushhal Kisan Yojana
Active - annual target or departmental sanction
Transition to certified/verified natural farming and on-farm inputs
Illustrative support: drums ₹750 each (max 3), cow-urine pit up to ₹8,000, indigenous cow 50% up to ₹25,000 plus transport up to ₹5,000; notified procurement support for natural produce.
Rates/procurement crops are notification-driven; verify the current season.
Agriculture Extension Officer / Block Agriculture Office
Register through Agriculture Department/ATMA natural-farming staff.
Quality testing certification IP and compliance
ZED assessment, certification, testing and handholding

Certification-cost subsidy 80% for micro, 60% for small and 50% for medium enterprises, plus an extra 10% for women/SC/ST-owned units and for units in NER, Himalayan states (Himachal Pradesh qualifies), LWE, island territories and aspirational districts, plus a further 5% for units in a SFURTI or MSE-CDP cluster. One-time joining reward of ₹10,000 on taking the ZED Pledge.
Use current portal package and approved providers; this replaces treating ISO reimbursement as a universal standalone scheme.
Agriculture Extension Officer / Block Agriculture Office
Register on ZED portal using Udyam details.

Exposure visits, training and transfer of improved agricultural technology
Programme-funded training/exposure; no standard direct cash ceiling.
Enabling support; participation depends on programme calendar.
Agriculture Extension Officer / Block Agriculture Office
Contact Agriculture Department/ATMA for scheduled programmes.

Competitive selection; not a universal reimbursement.

Apply through Startup Himachal/incubator when the seed-fund window is open.

Credit guarantee working capital and equity
Kisan Credit Card (KCC) / Modified Interest Subvention Scheme
Active - annual target or departmental sanction
Short-term crop production and eligible animal husbandry/fisheries working capital

KCC limit under the Modified Interest Subvention Scheme enhanced from ₹3 lakh to ₹5 lakh with effect from FY2025-26. Eligible short-term loans carry 7% p.a.; a 3% prompt repayment incentive brings the effective rate to 4%. Government pays lending institutions 1.5% interest subvention. Collateral-free agricultural loan limit is ₹2 lakh per borrower, effective 1 January 2025.
The ₹5 lakh KCC/MISS limit includes allied activities; interest benefit, drawing power and security still follow the current lender/RBI instructions.
Agriculture Extension Officer / Block Agriculture Office

Rural primary processing and collection infrastructure

Apply under the State Mission through DIC/Industries Department.
Food & Nutrition Security / National Food Security Mission
Active - annual target or departmental sanction
Rice, wheat, pulses, maize and nutri-cereals: demonstrations, seed, micronutrients and notified machinery
Component-wise subsidised seed, demonstrations, plant protection, micronutrients and machinery under the approved action plan; HP reported a ₹9.65 crore FY2025-26 programme.
No single percentage applies across all inputs; the district crop plan and cost norm control assistance.
Agriculture Extension Officer / Block Agriculture Office
Apply through the Agriculture Extension Officer under the notified crop/component and seasonal target.
HP Crop Diversification Promotion Project (JICA Phase II)
Irrigation, farm access, fencing, diversification and value-chain support in project areas
Support is delivered through approved subprojects and farmer groups; no single beneficiary-wide rate.
Not an open statewide reimbursement scheme.
Agriculture Extension Officer / Block Agriculture Office
Contact the project/Agriculture Department for selected locations and components.
Active - annual target or departmental sanction
Community water harvesting such as check dams and ponds
Government bears 100% of approved community work cost under departmental norms.
This is not a cash grant to an individual farmer.
Agriculture Extension Officer / Block Agriculture Office
Propose through Agriculture Department/block office; work is department-sanctioned.
Kisan Evam Khetihar Mazdoor Jeevan Suraksha Yojana
Active - annual target or departmental sanction
₹10,000–₹40,000 for specified injuries; ₹1 lakh for severe disability and ₹3 lakh for death, subject to rules.
This is accident compensation, not business capital assistance.
Agriculture Extension Officer / Block Agriculture Office
Submit claim promptly through Agriculture Department/revenue/authorised channel with incident evidence.
Active - annual target or departmental sanction
Farm inputs, cluster production, seed multiplication and agriculture-support components
Common notified input rates include 50% on seed of cereals/pulses/oilseeds/fodder and 25% on potato/ginger/turmeric; other components vary annually.
MKSY is an umbrella; use the current component circular, not a single blanket percentage.
Agriculture Extension Officer / Block Agriculture Office
Apply through local Agriculture Extension Officer/block office under the notified component.
Active - annual target or departmental sanction
State-approved innovation, infrastructure and value-chain projects
No universal individual percentage; benefit follows an approved State DPR/component.
Enabling/project umbrella, not a flat farmer subsidy.
Agriculture Extension Officer / Block Agriculture Office
Track HP Agriculture notifications/approved project calls.
Soil Health & Fertility / Soil Health Card
Active - annual target or departmental sanction
Soil testing, soil-health cards and balanced nutrient recommendations
Government-funded soil testing and soil-health card/advisory; HP's FY2025-26 programme budget was ₹3.92 crore. There is no standard cash payment to the farmer.
Laboratory coverage and sample collection are programme based; the card is advisory, not a subsidy sanction.
Agriculture Extension Officer / Block Agriculture Office
Contact the Agriculture Extension Officer or soil-testing laboratory for the district sampling schedule.
Insurance risk compensation and income support
Active - annual target or departmental sanction
Notified food/oilseed/commercial crops against insured perils
Farmer premium capped at 2% Kharif, 1.5% Rabi and 5% annual commercial/horticultural crops; balance actuarial premium subsidised by Government.
Voluntary participation, but crop/area/date and claim process are season-specific.
Agriculture Extension Officer / Block Agriculture Office
Enrol through notified insurer, bank or CSC before season cut-off.
Him Unnati / Him Krishi cluster programme
Cluster production, aggregation, services and market linkage
Need-based approved support through about 2,600 clusters; no single universal cash percentage.
Enabling programme; the sanctioned cluster DPR controls individual benefits.
Agriculture Extension Officer / Block Agriculture Office
Contact Agriculture Department to confirm whether the village/commodity cluster is selected.
Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana / Natural Farming component
Cluster conversion, inputs, certification/verification and marketing
Assistance follows current cluster guidelines and State action plan; no single standalone enterprise cap.
Avoid double-claiming the same cost under State natural-farming support.
Agriculture Extension Officer / Block Agriculture Office
Join an approved cluster through Agriculture Department.
PM-KUSUM / Saur Sinchai implementation in HP
Active - annual target or departmental sanction
Standalone solar agriculture pumps and notified solarisation components
85% assistance for small and marginal farmers and 80% for medium and large farmers on approved solar water-lifting/pumping systems, individual or community.
Original CSV's separate 60%/80% rows were not a reliable representation of HP's current assistance.
Agriculture Extension Officer / Block Agriculture Office
Apply through the HP AgriDBT portal (agridbt.hp.gov.in) or the dedicated PM-KUSUM portal (pmkusumagri.hp.gov.in) via the Block/District Agriculture Office.
Active - annual target or departmental sanction
Generally 40%–50% on notified equipment and benchmark cost; exact rate varies by beneficiary and machine.

Agriculture Extension Officer / Block Agriculture Office
Apply through Agriculture Department/DBT workflow before purchase.
Rajiv Gandhi Prakritik Kheti Khushhal Kisan Yojana
Active - annual target or departmental sanction
Transition to certified/verified natural farming and on-farm inputs
Illustrative support: drums ₹750 each (max 3), cow-urine pit up to ₹8,000, indigenous cow 50% up to ₹25,000 plus transport up to ₹5,000; notified procurement support for natural produce.
Rates/procurement crops are notification-driven; verify the current season.
Agriculture Extension Officer / Block Agriculture Office
Register through Agriculture Department/ATMA natural-farming staff.

Credit guarantee working capital and equity
Kisan Credit Card (KCC) / Modified Interest Subvention Scheme
Active - annual target or departmental sanction
Short-term crop production and eligible animal husbandry/fisheries working capital

KCC limit under the Modified Interest Subvention Scheme enhanced from ₹3 lakh to ₹5 lakh with effect from FY2025-26. Eligible short-term loans carry 7% p.a.; a 3% prompt repayment incentive brings the effective rate to 4%. Government pays lending institutions 1.5% interest subvention. Collateral-free agricultural loan limit is ₹2 lakh per borrower, effective 1 January 2025.
The ₹5 lakh KCC/MISS limit includes allied activities; interest benefit, drawing power and security still follow the current lender/RBI instructions.
Agriculture Extension Officer / Block Agriculture Office
Apply to bank/RRB/cooperative bank; use JanSamarth where enabled.
Active - annual target or departmental sanction
Kuhl/community flow irrigation and eligible individual wells
100% for approved community kuhl work; 50% subsidy for eligible individual bore/shallow wells.
Water availability, technical feasibility and cost norms apply.
Agriculture Extension Officer / Block Agriculture Office
Apply through Agriculture Department before construction.
Active - annual target or departmental sanction
Orchards, nurseries, protected cultivation, mushrooms, mechanisation and post-harvest components
In Himalayan states many private-sector components receive 50% of benchmark cost; some components range 40%–75%. Caps are component-specific.
Use the 2025 MIDH cost norm and current HP action plan; do not use a generic percentage for every component.
Agriculture Extension Officer / Block Agriculture Office
Apply through Horticulture Department under the approved Annual Action Plan.

Assistance is tiered by fencing type on the approved cost norm: solar fencing 80% for an individual and 85% for a group; composite fencing 70%; barbed wire / chain-link fencing 50%.
Sanction, design, vendor/specification and physical verification precede subsidy.
Agriculture Extension Officer / Block Agriculture Office
Apply to Agriculture Department before ordering/installation.

Export Promotion Mission – Niryat Protsahan finance interventions
Active - annual target or departmental sanction
Pre/post-shipment export credit, factoring and collateral support

Interest subvention of 2.75% p.a. on eligible rupee pre- and post-shipment export credit, capped at ₹50 lakh per IEC per financial year (same rate and cap for export factoring and e-commerce export credit). Apply through the export-credit bank and the notified Export Promotion Mission intervention; confirm product/country and claim-period eligibility.
Export Promotion Mission – TRACE and Niryat Disha market-readiness support
Active - annual target or departmental sanction
International testing, inspection, certification, branding, market access, logistics or warehousing

TRACE: assistance of 75% of actual cost net of taxes or ₹25 lakh, whichever is lower, for a certification on the notified Positive List, with an annual cap of ₹25 lakh per exporter. Related Niryat Disha interventions include LIFT freight reimbursement of up to 30% of actual cost capped at ₹20 lakh per IEC per year (Himalayan states are a covered low-export zone), FLOW overseas-warehousing support at the lower of 30% of approved project cost or ₹10 crore, and market-access support of up to ₹5 crore per event.
Only notified certifications, activities, destinations and claim periods qualify; avoid treating the Mission as one blanket reimbursement.

Active - annual target or departmental sanction

Export Promotion Mission – TRACE and Niryat Disha market-readiness support
Active - annual target or departmental sanction
International testing, inspection, certification, branding, market access, logistics or warehousing

TRACE: assistance of 75% of actual cost net of taxes or ₹25 lakh, whichever is lower, for a certification on the notified Positive List, with an annual cap of ₹25 lakh per exporter. Related Niryat Disha interventions include LIFT freight reimbursement of up to 30% of actual cost capped at ₹20 lakh per IEC per year (Himalayan states are a covered low-export zone), FLOW overseas-warehousing support at the lower of 30% of approved project cost or ₹10 crore, and market-access support of up to ₹5 crore per event.
Only notified certifications, activities, destinations and claim periods qualify; avoid treating the Mission as one blanket reimbursement.

Apply through the export-credit bank and the notified Export Promotion Mission intervention; confirm product/country and claim-period eligibility.

Active - annual target or departmental sanction
International testing, inspection, certification, branding, market access, logistics or warehousing

TRACE: assistance of 75% of actual cost net of taxes or ₹25 lakh, whichever is lower, for a certification on the notified Positive List, with an annual cap of ₹25 lakh per exporter. Related Niryat Disha interventions include LIFT freight reimbursement of up to 30% of actual cost capped at ₹20 lakh per IEC per year (Himalayan states are a covered low-export zone), FLOW overseas-warehousing support at the lower of 30% of approved project cost or ₹10 crore, and market-access support of up to ₹5 crore per event.
Only notified certifications, activities, destinations and claim periods qualify; avoid treating the Mission as one blanket reimbursement.
Use the notified Export Promotion Mission intervention or participating Export Promotion Council/implementing channel before incurring cost.

In HP/Himalayan area, subsidy commonly 50% of eligible project cost under current component norms; project ceiling and cost norm vary by crop/structure.
Use the latest operational guideline and 2026 amendment; old generic ceilings in the CSV were not dependable.
Apply online to NHB and obtain term-loan sanction before project execution as required.
Credit guarantee working capital and equity
Active - annual target or departmental sanction
Packhouse, grading, ripening, primary processing and eligible logistics
Component-wise subsidy and cost ceiling under current MIDH/NHB norms; HP generally receives Himalayan-area rate.
A generic 'integrated packhouse' row should be treated as this component, not a separate HP scheme.
Apply through NHB portal/bank under the relevant component.
Credit guarantee working capital and equity
Active - annual target or departmental sanction
Non-corporate, non-farm micro business and permitted allied activities
Shishu up to ₹50,000; Kishore above ₹50,000–₹5 lakh; Tarun above ₹5–₹10 lakh; Tarun Plus above ₹10–₹20 lakh only for borrowers who successfully repaid a Tarun loan.
No direct subsidy; interest is lender-determined. Guarantee is under the MUDRA/CGFMU framework, not ordinary CGTMSE.
Apply through bank, RRB, small finance bank, MFI/NBFC or JanSamarth where offered.
Active - annual target or departmental sanction
Sprayers, power tillers and notified orchard machinery
Subsidy on notified horticulture machinery at annual benchmark rates; percentage/ceiling varies by item and beneficiary.
Use the current machine-wise rate circular.
Apply through District Horticulture Office before purchase.
Active - annual target or departmental sanction
Anti-hail net system for eligible orchards
Assistance at the currently notified percentage and benchmark cost; annual ceiling/target applies.
MIDH and State components can overlap; claim only one aid stream per cost item.
Apply through Horticulture Department before installation.
Active - annual target or departmental sanction
Orchards, nurseries, protected cultivation, mushrooms, mechanisation and post-harvest components
In Himalayan states many private-sector components receive 50% of benchmark cost; some components range 40%–75%. Caps are component-specific.
Use the 2025 MIDH cost norm and current HP action plan; do not use a generic percentage for every component.
Apply through Horticulture Department under the approved Annual Action Plan.
Active - annual target or departmental sanction
Commercial mushroom production, spawn or compost unit

2025 MIDH cost norms for Himalayan states provide 50% assistance on benchmark costs; commercial component cost norms include mushroom production ₹30 lakh, spawn ₹20 lakh and compost ₹30 lakh, subject to component limits.
The original HP mushroom rates were not adequately sourced; use the current component guideline.
Apply through Horticulture Department or NHB route specified for project size.
Brownfield investment for recycling, resource efficiency and circularity

25% capital subsidy on eligible plant and machinery, maximum ₹12.5 lakh. The subsidy is computed on project cost up to ₹50 lakh; larger projects remain capped at ₹12.5 lakh. Brownfield projects of existing Udyam-registered MSEs only, in the 11 notified circular-economy sectors.
Brownfield/circular-economy eligibility and eligible asset list are decisive.
Apply through RAMP/SPICE portal with DPR and financing details.
Active - annual target or departmental sanction
Assistance follows annual plant, area and support-system cost norms; no single reliable statewide ceiling was published in the source reviewed.
Use current district allocation and technical package.
Apply through Horticulture Department after site suitability assessment.
New manufacturing or service unit by eligible Himachali youth

Investment subsidy: 25% general, 30% SC/ST, 35% women/divyang; eligible plant/machinery/equipment base up to ₹60 lakh. Interest subsidy 5% for 3 years on loan up to ₹60 lakh; project cost up to ₹1 crore.
Confirm activity, age and current district target before incurring expenditure.
Apply through the MMSY portal/District Industries Centre (DIC), then the financing bank.
Active - annual target or departmental sanction
55% of benchmark cost for small/marginal farmers and 45% for other farmers under national norms; HP annual implementation may add/adjust approved support.
Confirm whether the farm component is routed through Agriculture or Horticulture in the district.
Apply through Agriculture/Horticulture Department before installation.
New micro manufacturing or service enterprise
Project ceiling: ₹50 lakh manufacturing, ₹20 lakh service. General: 10% own contribution and 15% urban/25% rural subsidy. Special category: 5% contribution and 25% urban/35% rural subsidy.
Hill-area classification may support special-category rates; portal and bank decide final category.
Apply only on PMEGP e-portal; scrutiny by KVIC/KVIB/DIC and bank.
Insurance risk compensation and income support
Small exporters seeking buyer-default risk cover
Policy cover for eligible commercial and political risks, with maximum liability up to ₹2 crore under the Small Exporters Policy.
Cover percentage, waiting period, buyer limits, declarations and exclusions apply.
Apply to ECGC branch / online channel
Insurance risk compensation and income support
Weather Based Crop Insurance Scheme – horticulture crops
Active - annual target or departmental sanction
Notified fruit/horticulture crops against weather triggers
Farmer pays the notified subsidised premium; claim is trigger-based using weather data, not individual loss assessment.
Crop, area, insurer, premium and dates change each season.
Enrol through notified insurer/bank/CSC within seasonal cut-off.
Import of eligible capital goods at concessional or zero customs duty against prescribed export obligation under FTP rules.
Failure to meet export obligation creates duty and interest liability; check restricted/excluded items.
Government bears 90% of implementation consultant cost; indicative programme costs: Basic free, Intermediate ₹1.2 lakh, Advanced ₹2.4 lakh, with additional support for specified categories.
The benefit is for structured LEAN implementation, not machinery purchase.
Register on LEAN portal and use approved implementation consultant.
Manufacturers importing inputs for export production
Duty-free import of inputs physically incorporated in export product, subject to standard input-output norms or approved norms and export obligation.
Authorisation, actual-user, input nexus and export-obligation rules are strict.
The 2021–26 framework included market-development support; for certain fresh produce/flowers/eggs exporters, packaging assistance was 25% up to ₹5 lakh/year, subject to conditions.
Published FAS period ended 31-03-2026; no fresh successor window was verified at cutoff.
Check APEDA for successor guidelines before expenditure
Export Promotion Mission – Niryat Protsahan finance interventions
Active - annual target or departmental sanction
Pre/post-shipment export credit, factoring and collateral support

Interest subvention of 2.75% p.a. on eligible rupee pre- and post-shipment export credit, capped at ₹50 lakh per IEC per financial year (same rate and cap for export factoring and e-commerce export credit). Separate collateral-free guarantee intervention covers 85% for micro and small and 65% for medium enterprises, up to ₹10 crore per exporter per year. From 1 April 2026 Exim Bank, not RBI, processes interest-subvention claims.
Do not assume every export loan or shipment qualifies; RBI/lender instructions, exporter status and intervention dates control.
Apply through the export-credit bank and the notified Export Promotion Mission intervention; confirm product/country and claim-period eligibility.
Export Promotion Mission – TRACE and Niryat Disha market-readiness support
Active - annual target or departmental sanction
International testing, inspection, certification, branding, market access, logistics or warehousing

TRACE: assistance of 75% of actual cost net of taxes or ₹25 lakh, whichever is lower, for a certification on the notified Positive List, with an annual cap of ₹25 lakh per exporter. Related Niryat Disha interventions include LIFT freight reimbursement of up to 30% of actual cost capped at ₹20 lakh per IEC per year (Himalayan states are a covered low-export zone), FLOW overseas-warehousing support at the lower of 30% of approved project cost or ₹10 crore, and market-access support of up to ₹5 crore per event.
Only notified certifications, activities, destinations and claim periods qualify; avoid treating the Mission as one blanket reimbursement.
Use the notified Export Promotion Mission intervention or participating Export Promotion Council/implementing channel before incurring cost.
Active - annual target or departmental sanction
Disposal of eligible grade/quality produce through notified procurement centres

Market Intervention Scheme 2026-27 (approved July 2026): C-grade apple ₹12/kg, procurement 1 August-31 October 2026, up to 1.50 lakh MT; processing-grade mango ₹12/kg, 15 July-31 August 2026; citrus ₹12/kg for kinnow, malta and sangtra and ₹10/kg for galgal, 21 November 2026-15 February 2027. Procurement by HPMC, with HIMFED assisting on apple.
Seasonal and grade-specific; price and quantity limits must be rechecked each crop year.
Use notified HPMC/HIMFED/agency collection centres during the season.
Active - annual target or departmental sanction
ONDC onboarding, catalogue, account management, logistics and packaging support
Support includes onboarding/cataloguing up to ₹2,500 per MSE, account management up to ₹5,000, and notified logistics/packaging support.
Benefits are service/cost support, not unrestricted cash.
Apply through the TEAM/ONDC implementation channel when onboarding is open.
Active - annual target or departmental sanction
Central procuring entities target 25% annual procurement from MSEs, including sub-targets of 4% for SC/ST-owned and 3% for women-owned MSEs; tender benefits/exemptions apply under policy.
This is market access, not a cash subsidy; tender quality and technical conditions remain.
Register Udyam and GeM; respond to eligible tenders and use MSME Sambandh/Samadhan mechanisms.
RoDTEP – remission of duties and taxes on exported products
Electronic remission at notified product-specific rate and value cap; current schedule extended through 30 September 2026 for eligible exports.
Rates and exclusions are tariff-line specific; confirm treatment after 30-09-2026.
Declare RoDTEP claim in the shipping bill through Customs/ICEGATE
Quality testing certification IP and compliance
ZED assessment, certification, testing and handholding

Certification-cost subsidy 80% for micro, 60% for small and 50% for medium enterprises, plus an extra 10% for women/SC/ST-owned units and for units in NER, Himalayan states (Himachal Pradesh qualifies), LWE, island territories and aspirational districts, plus a further 5% for units in a SFURTI or MSE-CDP cluster. One-time joining reward of ₹10,000 on taking the ZED Pledge.
Use current portal package and approved providers; this replaces treating ISO reimbursement as a universal standalone scheme.
Register on ZED portal using Udyam details.

Assistance follows capacity, technology and cost norms; Himalayan-area rates apply where specified in current guidelines.
Cold storage and CA storage are components, not two universal fixed-cap schemes.
Seek technical appraisal, NHB application and bank sanction before construction.

Active - annual target or departmental sanction
Packhouse, grading, ripening, primary processing and eligible logistics

Active - annual target or departmental sanction
Sprayers, power tillers and notified orchard machinery
Subsidy on notified horticulture machinery at annual benchmark rates; percentage/ceiling varies by item and beneficiary.
Use the current machine-wise rate circular.
Apply through District Horticulture Office before purchase.
Active - annual target or departmental sanction
Anti-hail net system for eligible orchards
Assistance at the currently notified percentage and benchmark cost; annual ceiling/target applies.
MIDH and State components can overlap; claim only one aid stream per cost item.
Apply through Horticulture Department before installation.
Active - annual target or departmental sanction
Orchards, nurseries, protected cultivation, mushrooms, mechanisation and post-harvest components
In Himalayan states many private-sector components receive 50% of benchmark cost; some components range 40%–75%. Caps are component-specific.
Use the 2025 MIDH cost norm and current HP action plan; do not use a generic percentage for every component.
Apply through Horticulture Department under the approved Annual Action Plan.
Active - annual target or departmental sanction
Commercial mushroom production, spawn or compost unit

2025 MIDH cost norms for Himalayan states provide 50% assistance on benchmark costs; commercial component cost norms include mushroom production ₹30 lakh, spawn ₹20 lakh and compost ₹30 lakh, subject to component limits.
The original HP mushroom rates were not adequately sourced; use the current component guideline.
Apply through Horticulture Department or NHB route specified for project size.
Brownfield investment for recycling, resource efficiency and circularity

25% capital subsidy on eligible plant and machinery, maximum ₹12.5 lakh. The subsidy is computed on project cost up to ₹50 lakh; larger projects remain capped at ₹12.5 lakh. Brownfield projects of existing Udyam-registered MSEs only, in the 11 notified circular-economy sectors.
Brownfield/circular-economy eligibility and eligible asset list are decisive.
Apply through RAMP/SPICE portal with DPR and financing details.

Active - annual target or departmental sanction

Rashtriya Gokul Mission – breed multiplication/IVF/sex-sorted semen

Rashtriya Gokul Mission – breed multiplication/IVF/sex-sorted semen
Active - annual target or departmental sanction
Breed multiplication farm and advanced bovine breeding technologies

Under the revised mission (approved March 2025, outlay ₹3,400 crore up to FY2025-26): heifer rearing centres receive one-time assistance of 35% of capital cost; farmers receive up to 50% of the cost of sex-sorted semen; and 3% interest subvention is available on loans to induct high-genetic-merit IVF-born heifers. Most other components are 100% grant-in-aid. The earlier breed-multiplication-farm component offered 50% of project cost or ₹2 crore, whichever is lower, for a farm of at least 200 milch animals - confirm with DAHD whether that component is still open.
Component continuation/target must be confirmed after FY2025-26 allocation.
Use DAHD/RGM portal and State Animal Husbandry channel for the relevant component.

This is market access, not a cash subsidy; tender quality and technical conditions remain.
Register Udyam and GeM; respond to eligible tenders and use MSME Sambandh/Samadhan mechanisms.

ZED assessment, certification, testing and handholding

Use current portal package and approved providers; this replaces treating ISO reimbursement as a universal standalone scheme.
Register on ZED portal using Udyam details.

National Livestock Mission – Entrepreneurship Development Programme
Poultry, sheep/goat, piggery and fodder entrepreneurship components

50% capital subsidy on eligible project cost, with component ceilings: rural poultry (parent farm/hatchery) ₹25 lakh; sheep and goat breeding ₹50 lakh; piggery ₹30 lakh; feed and fodder entrepreneurship ₹50 lakh; fodder seed processing and grading ₹50 lakh. Balance is met through bank loan or self-finance; subsidy is released in two equal instalments through SIDBI.
Use the January 2025 component guideline for the exact unit size and cap.
Apply on NLM portal with bank sanction/DPR as prescribed.

Check portal/DAHD notice and lender before preparing a fresh application.

Livestock dairy poultry and animal enterprises
Rashtriya Gokul Mission – breed multiplication/IVF/sex-sorted semen
Active - annual target or departmental sanction
Breed multiplication farm and advanced bovine breeding technologies

Under the revised mission (approved March 2025, outlay ₹3,400 crore up to FY2025-26): heifer rearing centres receive one-time assistance of 35% of capital cost; farmers receive up to 50% of the cost of sex-sorted semen; and 3% interest subvention is available on loans to induct high-genetic-merit IVF-born heifers. Most other components are 100% grant-in-aid. The earlier breed-multiplication-farm component offered 50% of project cost or ₹2 crore, whichever is lower, for a farm of at least 200 milch animals - confirm with DAHD whether that component is still open.
Component continuation/target must be confirmed after FY2025-26 allocation.
Use DAHD/RGM portal and State Animal Husbandry channel for the relevant component.

National Livestock Mission – Entrepreneurship Development Programme
Poultry, sheep/goat, piggery and fodder entrepreneurship components

50% capital subsidy on eligible project cost, with component ceilings: rural poultry (parent farm/hatchery) ₹25 lakh; sheep and goat breeding ₹50 lakh; piggery ₹30 lakh; feed and fodder entrepreneurship ₹50 lakh; fodder seed processing and grading ₹50 lakh. Balance is met through bank loan or self-finance; subsidy is released in two equal instalments through SIDBI.
Use the January 2025 component guideline for the exact unit size and cap.
Apply on NLM portal with bank sanction/DPR as prescribed.

Active - annual target or departmental sanction
Upgrade an existing pharma plant to Revised Schedule M and/or WHO-GMP

20% of eligible investment for turnover below ₹50 crore; 15% for ₹50 crore to below ₹250 crore; 10% for ₹250 crore to below ₹500 crore; maximum incentive ₹2 crore per unit (raised from ₹1 crore by corrigendum of 17 September 2024). Indian pre-clinical study, clinical investigation, PMCF or new-IVD performance evaluation

Reimbursement of 25% of expenditure in every category, subject to: pre-clinical (animal) studies up to ₹2 crore; clinical investigation up to ₹5 crore; post-market clinical follow-up up to ₹1 crore; in-vitro diagnostic performance evaluation up to ₹1 crore.

Project ceiling ₹20 lakh for an individual (₹25 lakh for an exceptionally successful venture) and ₹100 lakh for a group of at least 5 trained persons. Subsidy is credit-linked and requires the venture to deliver extension services.
Confirm current project-cost norm and training eligibility before relying on the ceiling.

Verification Notes — scope, deletions, gaps and limits of this pass

All 182 rows of Scheme Master were reviewed. Every row carrying a hard number — a subsidy percentage, a ceiling, an interest rate, an eligibility threshold or a date — was checked against the issuing department's guideline, notification, PIB release or scheme portal. Rows that deliberately state no universal rate ("component-specific", "follows the approved DPR") make no falsifiable claim and were reviewed for status and source rather than re-costed. Component Norms was spot-checked against the MIDH Operational Guidelines 2025; Legacy & Closed, Start Here and the cross-sheet references were checked in full.

The workbook is internally sound. There are no duplicate Scheme IDs or duplicate scheme names; all 6,767 Sector-Scheme Map rows point to real sector and scheme IDs; every one of the 382 catalogue sectors has at least one mapping; and the denormalised copies of scheme data in Business Navigator and Sector-Scheme Map matched Scheme Master exactly before this pass. Six schemes are unmapped — all six are HPIIP 2019 rows, which is deliberate. Those copies have been refreshed wherever a Scheme Master cell changed, so the sheets still agree.
3. Claims deleted because no official source supports them

Per instruction, figures that could not be tied to an official source were removed rather than left in place. Each is logged in Corrections Log with the reason. They are:
• PM SVANidhi — the "UPI-linked credit facility up to ₹30,000" and the flat "7% interest subsidy". No official document states a limit for the RuPay card, and the 7% subvention belonged to the 2020 scheme and is not restated anywhere in the 2025 restructuring papers.
• MSE SPICE — "project cost up to ₹2 crore". SIDBI's own FAQ and brochure both set the subsidy-computation base at ₹50 lakh.
• Micro Credit Card — "75% guarantee coverage". Unsourced, and inconsistent with CGTMSE's 85% cover for micro credit up to ₹5 lakh.
• SRI Fund — "Budget 2026-27 added ₹2,000 crore". An additional allocation is confirmed; the amount is not.
• NSIC Raw Material Assistance — "rates effective 10 July 2026 range from 9.25% to 10.75%". No circular of that date was locatable; the last documented schedule (1 July 2025) is 8.75%–10.25%.
• DRDO TDF — "projects above ₹10 crore funded up to 70%". Both the Ministry of Defence release and DDP's scheme page state a single level of up to 90%.
• SMDI Clinical Studies — "applicants with turnover up to ₹10 crore may receive up to 70%". The SMDI operational guidelines of 8 November 2024 apply a flat 25% with no size differential.
• RPTUAS — the "₹1 crore" minimum turnover. Eligibility is stated as turnover below ₹500 crore, with no floor.
4. The corrections that change a decision

Six errors would have changed what someone did:
• MCGS-MSME had two percentages transposed — guarantee coverage is 60% and the minimum machinery share of project cost is 75%, not the other way round. A project designed to the 60% machinery test would fail eligibility.
• FIDF promoter contribution was recorded as "at least 5%"; it is at least 20% margin money. A promoter would have been short by 15% of project cost.
• HPIIP 2019 was marked "existing beneficiaries only". The policy has been extended repeatedly past its 31 December 2025 cutoff and was reported on 18 August 2026 as running to 12 October 2026 — new units are still eligible.
• The Rajiv Gandhi Swarozgar bus scheme was described at Stage III terms (30%, 18–42 seater, electric only). Phase-IV, announced 29 June 2026, gives 50% on e-buses and 30% on diesel buses, requires a minimum 32 seats, and adds a five-year monthly operational incentive.
• Export Promotion Mission TRACE support is 75% of eligible cost, not 60%.
• PM E-DRIVE's electric two-wheeler demand incentive closed on 31 July 2026 — before the workbook's own cutoff date — and the e-three-wheeler incentive has been halved to ₹12,500.
5. Central schemes whose sanctioned period has lapsed

Several central schemes were sanctioned only up to FY2025-26 and that period ended on 31 March 2026. Their portals often remain live, which is why they read as active. Statuses have been changed to "Fresh window closed" for AHIDF, PMMSY and FIDF, and a period note added to iDEX. PMFME is different — it has been extended through September 2026 with a five-year continuation proposal pending, so it is now marked active with a dated caution. In every case the underlying benefit terms were verified as correct; it is only the availability that has moved.

Two 2026 measures relevant to this guide are absent from Scheme Master. They were not inserted because adding rows would require rebuilding the sector mappings, but they are worth adding deliberately:
• SME Growth Fund — ₹10,000 crore, announced in Budget 2026-27.
• A revamped Stand-Up India for SC/ST and women entrepreneurs, stated in the Lok Sabha on 16 March 2026 to be under drafting. The Legacy & Closed entry has been updated to reflect this.
7. Limits of this pass — read before relying on the file

• Himachal-specific livestock, fisheries and horticulture rows (Him Kukkut Palan, Krishak Bakri Palan, breeding-ram subsidy, BPL cattle ration, Uttam Pashu Puraskar, backyard poultry, HP Fisheries Risk Fund and the departmental budget figures) rest on the HP Economic Survey 2025-26. That is an official document but a secondary one for operational detail; the department's own sanction order should be seen before committing money. They were left unchanged because nothing contradicted them.
• Component Norms was verified by sampling. The nursery norms, the high-density and ultra-high-density apple norms and the Himalayan-state 50% assistance rate all matched the MIDH Operational Guidelines 2025 exactly, so the sheet is treated as sound; but Annexure V could not be read line-by-line through an automated fetch, so the remaining rows are not individually confirmed.
• The tiered fencing rates under Mukhya Mantri Khet Sanrakshan Yojana come from contemporary reporting of the scheme launch, not from a live departmental page. Confirm with the District Agriculture Officer.
• Scheme windows move. Every date in this workbook is a snapshot at 2026-08-23.

Three schemes were renamed in this pass (the fencing scheme, the Rajiv Gandhi Swarozgar bus scheme and the small-shopkeeper scheme). Their Scheme IDs still carry the old name slug — for example SCH-RAJIV-GANDHI-LAGHU-DUKANDAR-SUKH-KALYAN-YO-A74FFA now belongs to the Mukhya Mantri Laghu Dukandar Kalyan Yojana. This is deliberate: the ID is the join key used by Sector-Scheme Map, and rewriting it would break any reference held outside this workbook. Read the ID as an opaque key, not as the scheme's name.

sheets.name: Legacy & Closed
headers: Why not a normal current scheme

values: Why not a normal current scheme
Original scheme period ended 31 March 2025; a revamped scheme was announced but not yet notified as of the verification date

The scheme's notified period ran to 31 March 2025 and lapsed. On 16 March 2026 the Finance Minister stated in the Lok Sabha that a revamped Stand-Up India for SC/ST and women entrepreneurs was being drafted; the original ₹10 lakh-₹1 crore bank-loan structure is expected to carry forward but the revamped scheme had not been notified as of verification.
Use PMEGP, MMSY, PMMY, CGTMSE/SCLCSS or targeted corporation finance as applicable.
Extended - the 2019 policy has been kept alive past its 31 December 2025 cutoff pending a new industrial policy

The policy lapsed on 31 December 2025 but the State has extended it repeatedly while the successor industrial policy remains unnotified - most recently, as reported on 18 August 2026, up to 12 October 2026. It is therefore still available to units commencing commercial production within the extended window, but the end date moves and must be checked before committing investment.

Confirm the live end date with the Single Window Clearance Authority / Department of Industries before committing investment, and in parallel examine MMSY, Startup Himachal, State Mission on Food Processing and central schemes.
Superseded/closed as a general current scheme
Do not use old 15%/₹15 lakh CLCSS data as a current general entitlement.
SC/ST-owned MSEs should examine current SCLCSS; all MSEs can examine ZED, LEAN, GIFT, SPICE and other technology schemes.
SIDBI reports ARISE, SPEED Plus and PRATHAM branch products were merged into SPEED.
Ask SIDBI for current SPEED/equipment-finance terms.
The old Rural Godown/Gramin Bhandaran branding should not be treated as a live standalone scheme.
Check AMI/AIF/NHB/MIDH; verify a live post-31 March 2026 AMI sanction window.
Do not prepare a fresh DIDF application.
Check AHIDF, but confirm a fresh post-31 March 2026 window.
National Scheme of Welfare of Fishermen
Insurance, saving-cum-relief and related welfare now operate through PMMSY/State implementation.
Use PMMSY/PM-MKSSY and HP Fisheries Department current enrolments.
RIDF finances State/public rural infrastructure; an individual MSME/farm unit does not apply as a beneficiary enterprise.
Use AIF, NCDC or the relevant direct beneficiary scheme.
Indirect fund/equity route; original row not a direct subsidy
Fund availability and investee selection are manager-led and should not be represented as a fixed beneficiary grant.
Check NSFDC/PM-SURAJ and current fund manager/Startup India equity routes.
Fresh applications after 31 March 2026 not confirmed
Official page states scheme approval through 31 March 2026; legacy/committed cases may continue.
Confirm new notification with DAHD and lender before relying on it.
Fresh proposals after 31 March 2026 not confirmed
Official published extension ran through 31 March 2026.
Check FIDF portal/Department of Fisheries for a new extension.
Benefit architecture remains relevant for approved/legacy cases, but original programme period was through FY2025-26.
Check the HP nodal agency and portal for a live intake.
PRIP – Promotion of Research and Innovation in Pharma-MedTech
Round 1 closed; no further round presently planned

The portal closed on 19 November 2025. The Department subsequently stated that, because the scheme closes in March 2027 and needs a one-year gestation period, no further application rounds are under consideration.
For a new innovation examine BIRAC BIG, MSME Innovative, iDEX/TDF where relevant, Startup Himachal, or future successor notifications.
The scheme is paying incentive to selected applicants; no general fresh application window was located for a new unit in August 2026.
New pharma units should examine RPTUAS if an upgrade window reopens, the Haroli Bulk Drug Park, general MSME finance, and future DoP calls.
Current releases report implementation/disbursement but no fresh general application window.
Examine SMDI MIS-RID, clinical-study support, cluster facilities and future DoP notices.
Current invitation closed / approved projects continue

The most recent located invitation was dated 19 February 2026 for specified eligible products; no open August 2026 window was located. Incentive continues for approved applicants through the scheme period.
Monitor the Department of Pharmaceuticals scheme page for another product-specific invitation and consider the Haroli Bulk Drug Park.
Himachal Pradesh Medical Device Park, Nalagarh
Infrastructure under development; some works on hold

HP Economic Survey 2025-26 states operation/management activity is under implementation but certain civil works are on hold due to shortage of funds. It is an industrial-location project, not a universal cash scheme.
Ask HP Industries/implementing corporation for the current plot-allotment notice and written concessions before relying on the park.
Announced in Union Budget 2026-27; operational criteria not yet located
A budget announcement is not an investible scheme until the fund structure, manager, eligibility and application route are notified.
Use the active SRI Fund/Daughter Fund route or ordinary equity/debt meanwhile; monitor MSME Ministry notifications.
Revamped Pharmaceutical Technology Upgradation Assistance Scheme (RPTUAS)

As of 4 August 2026, a temporary restriction remained while extension was considered; 21 HP applications were pending. Drug licences, Schedule M/WHO-GMP certification and two-stage verification apply.
Monitor the Department of Pharmaceuticals SPI page/portal and obtain confirmation that fresh intake has reopened before committing upgrade expenditure.
Assistance to Pharmaceutical Industry for Common Facilities (API-CF)
Latest located fresh window closed in January 2025; the 4 August 2026 official update reported no HP proposal pending under API-CF. Not an individual-unit grant.
Form/strengthen the SPV and monitor the SPI scheme page for a fresh API-CF application window before preparing the final DPR.
SMDI – Marginal Investment Scheme for Reducing Import Dependence (MIS-RID)
The June/July 2026 call closed on 24 July 2026. Incentive follows commissioning and verification; land is excluded and device/product eligibility is narrow.
Use the SMDI portal only against a live notice and obtain product/category confirmation before investment.
SMDI – Medical Device Clinical Studies Support
The July 2026 call is closed. Funding does not replace regulatory approval and is reimbursed only for admissible Indian studies and verified milestones.
Secure CDSCO/ethics and other required permissions, then apply through SMDI only during a live call.
SMDI – Common Facilities for Medical Device Clusters
The July 2026 proposal window has closed. It is not a grant to one factory and requires shared-access governance and sustainable operations.
Prepare a cluster DPR and apply through SMDI only under a live call.
Official approval was stated through 31 March 2026; as of verification, a fresh post-March-2026 sanction window was not confirmed.
Check portal/DAHD notice and lender before preparing a fresh application.
Fisheries and Aquaculture Infrastructure Development Fund (FIDF)
Published extension ran through 31 March 2026; fresh proposal status after that date was not confirmed.
Check current FIDF portal/Department of Fisheries before a fresh proposal.
PM Formalisation of Micro Food Processing Enterprises (PMFME)
Original implementation period was through FY2025-26; portal/legacy processing continues, but a fresh FY2026-27 intake was not confirmed in the source reviewed.
Check HP PMFME/DIC and portal for a currently open intake.
HPIIP 2019 – MSME land, shed, stamp duty and CLU incentives

The amended policy limits incentives to qualifying units commencing commercial production on or before 31-12-2025. No official extension was found as of the verification date; do not model this as a fresh-project incentive.
Claim through Industries Department / Single Window with eligibility certificate
Only policy-period beneficiaries; verify sanction, location category and claim deadlines.
Claim through District Industries Centre / Industries Department
HPIIP 2019 – transport subsidy for B and C areas
Fresh eligibility window ended 31-12-2025; turnover and freight definitions require official assessment.
December 2023 amendment applies; fresh policy eligibility closed after 31-12-2025.
Claim through Industries and State Taxes departments
HPIIP 2019 – technology, quality, EHS and green-fuel support
Fresh eligibility closed; separate environmental approvals remain mandatory.
Claim through Industries Department with technical approvals
HPIIP 2019 – employment, export, patent and SME listing support
Employment route requires more than 80% Himachalis and prescribed regular-employment thresholds; fresh policy eligibility ended 31-12-2025.
Rajiv Gandhi Laghu Dukandar Sukh Kalyan Yojana
The policy is reported in the Economic Survey, but a current public application window and complete operative guidelines were not located.
Confirm current intake with District Industries Centre / lender
